Sorting is required if exact distance ordering is needed, though simple counting often suffices for parity [S4, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that `hit_xs` (intersection X-coordinates) are sorted to correct precision-induced ordering errors. It further explains that the inside status is determined by counting intersections to the right of a voxel center. This counting method relies on the intersections being ordered by distance (X-coordinate) to accurately determine parity (inside/outside). Therefore, sorting is required for the exact distance ordering needed for the parity check to work correctly. The claim that 'simple counting often suffices for parity' is supported by the fact that the algorithm uses a simple parity check (`intersections_to_right % 2 != 0`) on the sorted list, rather than a more complex distance-based classification for the inside/outside determination itself (though SDF is computed separately). The core logic for the topological inside/outside status is indeed simple parity counting on the sorted distances.
